# 2.5 Linear Diophantine equations and the Chinese remainder theorem

Phase 2 (Mathematics I), target rating 1400–1700. Bank status: short.

## Patterns

### Linear equations in two integer unknowns (`diophantine`)

Decide whether a·x + b·y = c has integer solutions, find one, list all of them, or find the best one in a range, with extended Euclid.

**Works because:** The solutions exist exactly when gcd(a, b) divides c, and all of them are spaced by (b/g, −a/g).

### One congruence with any modulus (`linear-congruence`)

Solve a·x ≡ b (mod m) when m is not prime, or find when a periodic walk first hits a target, by reducing to a·x + m·y = b.

**Works because:** A solution exists exactly when gcd(a, m) divides b, and then the solutions are one residue class modulo m / gcd(a, m).

### Systems of congruences (`crt`)

Merge x ≡ r1 (mod m1) and x ≡ r2 (mod m2) into one congruence modulo lcm(m1, m2), when the moduli are not coprime.

**Works because:** The two congruences agree modulo gcd(m1, m2); then the solution is unique modulo the lcm.
